cases.description: All instrument, calibration, installation, sample and derived evidence dependencies are current.
A calibration certificate is revoked; only its transitive measurement dependants are invalidated.
An instrument firmware/configuration revision is superseded and its dependent evidence is invalidated.
An installation is changed; only spatially dependent descendants become invalidated.
A purpose profile is corrected; the raw observation remains current but its decision claim is invalidated.
An independent assay is revoked; the raw sample remains current while the dependent claim is invalidated.
A raw sample is superseded; all derived and claim descendants are invalidated.
A calibration expires and cannot remain current just because a downstream status flag says current.
An instrument identity becomes unknown; its dependent evidence cannot remain current.
Independent calibration events invalidate two branches without cross-contaminating one another.
Node and edge array permutation produces the same canonical topological order and result.
A dependency edge with a mismatched parent digest is rejected.
A dependency edge with a mismatched parent revision is rejected.
A dangling dependency is rejected.
A self-dependency is rejected.
A duplicate dependency edge is rejected.
The same node ID with changed content digest is a conflict, not an overwrite.
An exact duplicate node identity/revision/digest is idempotent and canonicalized once.
A two-node dependency cycle is rejected.
A longer three-node dependency cycle is rejected.
A repeated event ID is rejected rather than silently choosing one payload.
An invalidation event bound to a stale node digest is rejected.
A previously superseded parent invalidates descendants even without a new event.
A corrected uncertainty budget invalidates the quality claim but preserves its raw sample.
A derivation method change invalidates derived output and dependent claim, not the source observation.
Rights revocation on one sample branch does not invalidate another room or instrument branch.
Two independent source changes are applied in one deterministic graph evaluation.
Repeated canonicalization of independently shuffled input arrays has an identical semantic output.
